items.prompt: White to move. One black piece can be captured for free. Find the move.

claims.statement: Rxd6 wins the bishop and White keeps the rook.
No black piece defends the bishop.

hints: Which black pieces can a white piece capture?
A capture is free when nothing can recapture. Which black piece has no defender?
The rook on the d-file can take the bishop on d6.
items.explain: Nothing guards the bishop on d6, so the rook takes it and cannot be taken back: White wins 3 points.

items.prompt: Should White take the knight on e5 with the bishop? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxe5 wins the knight and White keeps the bishop.
No black piece guards e5.

hints: Can White capture the knight at all?
After the capture, could Black capture the bishop back?
items.explain: Nothing defends the knight, so Black cannot recapture. White wins a whole knight (3 points) for nothing.

items.prompt: The same bishop can take a pawn on e5. Should White take it? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxe5 loses the bishop for a pawn.
The pawn on d6 guards e5.

hints: Can White capture the pawn? Yes. So ask the second question: what happens next?
Which black piece could take the bishop back on e5?
The pawn on d6 guards e5.
items.explain: The pawn on d6 guards e5. After Bxe5 dxe5, White has traded a bishop (3 points) for a pawn (1 point): White is 2 points behind.

items.prompt: White thinks about taking the pawn on d5 with the queen. Black will recapture if it can. After the captures, what has happened to White's points?

claims.statement: Qxd5 cxd5 loses the queen for a pawn.
The pawn on c6 guards d5.

hints: Is the pawn on d5 guarded?
Add up what White gives up and what White takes.
The queen is worth 9 points, the pawn 1.
items.explain: The pawn on c6 takes the queen back. White gives up 9 points for 1.

items.prompt: White thinks about taking the knight on e5 with the bishop. Black will recapture if it can. After the captures, what has happened to White's points?

claims.statement: Bxe5 dxe5 is an even swap.
The pawn on d6 guards e5.

hints: Is the knight guarded?
Add up what White gives up and what White takes.
A bishop and a knight are each worth 3 points.
items.explain: The pawn on d6 takes the bishop back. White gives 3 points and gets 3: an even trade.

items.prompt: White thinks about taking the pawn on e5 with the knight. After the captures, what has happened to White's points?

claims.statement: Nxe5 wins at least a pawn.
No black piece guards e5.

hints: Is the pawn guarded?
If nothing can recapture, what does White gain?
items.explain: Nothing guards the pawn on e5, so White simply wins it.

items.prompt: White thinks about taking the rook on e6 with the knight. The pawn on f7 guards e6 and will recapture. After the captures, what has happened to White's points?

claims.statement: Nxe6 fxe6 wins 2 points for White.
The pawn on f7 guards e6.

hints: The rook is guarded. Does that mean White should not take it?
Add up what White gives up and what White takes.
A knight is worth 3 points and a rook 5.
items.explain: Black recaptures the knight, but White took a rook: White gives 3 points and gets 5. A guarded piece can still be worth taking when it is worth more than the piece you give up.

items.prompt: Black has a queen and White has only a rook, with the same pawns. White to move: find White's best move.

claims.statement: Rd8 is checkmate.

hints: Forget the points for a moment. Where is Black's king, and what stands next to it?
Black's king has pawns on f7, g7 and h7 in front of it. Which rank is it on?
A rook on the back rank would attack the king along the rank.
items.explain: Rd8 is checkmate: the rook attacks the king, the pawns block its escape, and nothing can capture the rook or block. Black has more points, but checkmate ends the game.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece that is loose (attacked, and not defended). Kings do not count.

claims.statement: The pawn on b6 is the only loose black piece.
Two white pieces attack the bishop on d5.
One black piece defends the bishop on d5.

hints: First find every black piece that a white piece attacks. Then check each one for a defender.
The bishop on d5 is attacked twice, but look at e6.
The pawn on b6 is attacked by the queen. Does any black piece defend it?
items.explain: The bishop on d5 is attacked twice but the pawn on e6 defends it, so it is not loose. The pawn on b6 is attacked by the queen and nothing defends it: it is the only loose piece.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece that is loose (attacked, and not defended). Kings do not count.

claims.statement: The pawn on b7 and the bishop on d5 are the loose black pieces.

hints: Find every black piece that a white piece attacks. The queen attacks along lines.
For each attacked piece, ask: could a black piece take back on that square?
Two pieces on the queen's lines have no defender.
items.explain: The queen attacks both the bishop on d5 and the pawn on b7, and no black piece defends either one. Both are loose.

items.prompt: White to move. The black bishop attacks White's queen. How many of White's pieces are loose? (Attacked, and not defended; kings do not count.)

claims.statement: No white piece is both attacked and undefended.
The bishop on d5 attacks the queen on b3.
The pawn on a2 defends the queen on b3.

hints: Make a list of the white pieces that Black attacks.
For each one, find a white defender.
Look at what defends the queen on b3.
items.explain: The bishop attacks the queen, but the pawn on a2 defends her, and no other white piece is attacked at all. Attacked is not the same as loose: no white piece is loose.

items.prompt: How many white pieces and pawns attack the black knight on e5?

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack e5.

hints: Pawns attack the two squares diagonally in front of them.
Knights attack the squares an L-jump away.
The pawn on f4 and the knight on f3 both reach e5.
items.explain: The pawn on f4 attacks e5 diagonally, and the knight on f3 attacks e5 with an L-jump: two attackers.

items.prompt: How many black pieces and pawns defend the black knight on e5?

claims.statement: One black piece defends e5.

hints: A piece defends a square if it could capture there after an enemy piece lands on it.
Black pawns attack diagonally downward.
Look at d6.
items.explain: Only the pawn on d6 could take back on e5: one defender.

items.prompt: Two attackers against one defender. White starts by taking with the pawn on f4. Black takes back, and White takes again. Is White ahead in the end? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Starting with the pawn wins 3 points.
Two attackers.
One defender.

hints: Add up the swaps one at a time: first capture, recapture, last capture.
The pawn takes the knight (3). The pawn on d6 takes the pawn (1). Then the knight takes the pawn (1).
White gains 3 + 1, loses 1.
items.explain: The pawn takes a knight (+3), the pawn on d6 takes the pawn (-1), the knight takes the pawn on e5 (+1): White ends 3 points ahead. The cheapest attacker went first.

items.prompt: Two attackers against one defender again, but now the attackers are a knight and a bishop and the target is a pawn. White starts with a capture on e5. Is White ahead in the end? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Starting the captures on e5 leaves White behind.
Two attackers.
One defender.

hints: Count the swaps again: first capture, recapture, last capture. What is each piece worth?
The first capturer is a knight (3). The target is a pawn (1).
The knight takes a pawn (+1), the pawn takes the knight (-3), the bishop takes a pawn (+1).
items.explain: More attackers than defenders did not help. White gives a knight (3) for a pawn, then wins a second pawn: 3 given, 2 won. The first piece to capture was worth more than the target.

items.prompt: White thinks about taking the knight on d5 with the bishop. Black will recapture if it can. After the captures, what has happened to White's points?

claims.statement: Bxd5 wins the knight.
One attacker.
No defenders.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of the knight.
With no defender, nothing can take back.
items.explain: One attacker, no defenders: the bishop takes the knight and nothing recaptures. White is 3 points ahead.

items.prompt: White thinks about taking the knight on e5 with the bishop. Black will recapture if it can. After the captures, what has happened to White's points?

claims.statement: Bxe5 dxe5 is an even swap.
One attacker.
One defender.

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders.
One attacker, one defender: after the swap nothing is left to capture. What did each side lose?
items.explain: One attacker against one defender: the bishop (3) takes a knight (3) and the pawn takes the bishop (3). Nobody is ahead.

items.prompt: White thinks about starting the captures on e5, with either the knight or the bishop. Black will recapture whenever it can. After all the captures, what has happened to White's points?

claims.statement: Two attackers.
Two defenders.
Nxe5 leaves White behind.
Bxe5 leaves White behind.

hints: Count the attackers of e5, then the defenders. Are the numbers equal?
Who has to capture first? That piece is the first one in danger.
White offers a piece for a pawn before getting anything back.
items.explain: Equal numbers favour the defender. White's first capture wins only a pawn, and a piece is taken in return. Whoever starts a capture on a square with as many defenders as attackers loses material first.
